args.sql:
WITH o AS (SELECT subtotal FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND ordered_at < '2026-01-01'),
b AS (SELECT CASE WHEN subtotal < 500 THEN 'under $5' WHEN subtotal < 1000 THEN '$5 to $10' WHEN subtotal < 2000 THEN '$10 to $20' ELSE '$20 or more' END band, subtotal FROM o)
SELECT band, COUNT(*) n, SUM(subtotal)/100.0 sales, SUM(subtotal)*1.0/(SELECT SUM(subtotal) FROM o) share, (SELECT MAX(ordered_at) FROM orders) mx, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE subtotal IS NULL) nulls
FROM b GROUP BY band ORDER BY MIN(subtotal)

WITH o AS (SELECT subtotal FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND ordered_at < '2026-01-01'),
b AS (SELECT CASE WHEN subtotal < 500 THEN 'under $5' WHEN subtotal < 1000 THEN '$5 to $10' WHEN subtotal < 2000 THEN '$10 to $20' ELSE '$20 or more' END band, subtotal FROM o)
SELECT band, COUNT(*) n, SUM(subtotal)/100.0 sales, SUM(subtotal)*1.0/(SELECT SUM(subtotal) FROM o) AS sh, (SELECT MAX(ordered_at) FROM orders) mx, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE subtotal IS NULL) AS nn
FROM b GROUP BY band ORDER BY MIN(subtotal)

args.message:
I grouped all 408,306 orders from calendar year 2025 by their pre-tax value (subtotal, converted from cents to dollars). Each band includes its lower limit and stops just below its upper one, so a $5.00 order is in "$5 to $10". Total 2025 pre-tax sales were $4,296,716.

| Band | Orders | Sales | Share of sales |
|---|---|---|---|
| under $5 | 60,191 | $229,504 | 5.3% |
| $5 to $10 | 232,467 | $1,401,521 | 32.6% |
| $10 to $20 | 71,778 | $1,118,561 | 26.0% |
| $20 or more | 43,870 | $1,547,130 | 36.0% |

The $5–$10 band has the most orders, but orders of $20 or more bring in the largest share of sales. The table I submitted gives each share as an exact fraction.
